assets.generationPrompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: original horizontal Matkakirja catalogue illustration, 16:9, intended final size 1600 × 900.
Create a single camera-real photograph of an old, worn wooden Nine Men's Morris board resting flat on a wooden table in a medieval stone room. No reference image is used. The board is fully visible, centered and safely inside the frame; an elevated almost top-down camera makes its precise geometry legible, while the distant stone room is softly out of focus. Warm low side light from a window, quiet natural muted brown tones, realistic wood pores, worn incised grooves, small imperfect circular wooden counters, gentle photographic depth of field.
The board's game graph is exact: THREE concentric complete square outlines. Each square has EIGHT legal stations: its four corners and the midpoint of each side, giving exactly 24 stations. Connect the three squares ONLY at the four side midpoints with four short straight cardinal connector segments. The connectors stop at the innermost square. The empty area INSIDE the innermost square contains absolutely no lines, cross, dot, decoration or counters. No diagonal lines. No full central cross. No additional squares or stations. Small round incised dots mark the stations not hidden by counters.
Exactly FOUR dark round wooden counters occupy the FOUR corner stations of the OUTERMOST square. Exactly FOUR light round wooden counters occupy the FOUR corner stations of the MIDDLE square. All eight counters sit precisely on these legal stations, no floating counter and no counter between stations. The innermost square is empty. This is a possible game in progress.
Make the scene look physically photographed with an ordinary high-quality camera: wood and stone have authentic irregular textures and natural highlights. Not an illustration, not watercolor, not a CGI render. No HDR, no oversaturation, no dramatic cinematic color grading.
No hands or people, no faces. No lettering, numbers, labels, symbols, logos, watermark or image border. The precise square-and-midpoint game geometry is the central subject.

Create a single natural camera-real air-to-air photograph of a small 1910–1920-era wooden and fabric biplane flying above a sea of soft foamy clouds. Far mountain summits rise on the distant horizon. The ENTIRE aircraft is in the central part of the frame with generous breathing room around both wing tips, tail and nose; crop-safe, approximately 60 percent of the image width. A slightly elevated three-quarter side view clearly shows two separate horizontal fabric wings, wooden interplane struts and fine rigging wires, the slim wooden-and-linen fuselage, simple tailplane and fixed undercarriage. Authentic period wood and taut cream linen materials with restrained natural wear, a small propeller with physically plausible rotational motion blur. A generic anonymous period biplane, no specific national or commercial aircraft identity.
Golden-hour natural sunlight gently warms the linen and wing surfaces, with realistic soft shadows, pale sky, muted warm cream and subdued blue-gray cloud shadows. Distant mountains and lower clouds recede naturally into atmospheric haze. It should look like an ordinary high-quality airborne photograph, with realistic scale, materials, perspective, light and photographic texture.
The small open cockpit is dark and does not reveal any person, face or human figure. Aircraft surfaces are entirely plain unmarked natural linen and wood: absolutely NO national insignia, roundels, crosses, flags, logos, registration codes, letters, numbers, symbols or decorative markings anywhere on wings, tail or fuselage. No lettering in the clouds or scenery. No text, watermark or image border.
No HDR, no oversaturation, no dramatic cinematic grading, no painting, no watercolor, no toy model, no CGI render. Emphasize believable physical early aviation and natural golden-hour photography.
